items.title: Opinion: AI cannot replace being human – The Battalion
items.summary: I understand the appeal. College is busy. Between classes, jobs, extracurriculars, leadership positions and trying to maintain some semblance of a social life, there are never enough hours in the day. AI makes things easier. It can generate an outline, rewrite a paragraph, summarize a reading or produce an entire essay before you have even finished your Celsius. But convenience does not necessarily facilitate education. [...] There is also something to be said about individuality. AI can generate an argument, imitate a writing style or suggest a creative direction, but our perspectives are developed through our own experiences, disagreements, mistakes and interpretations. The things that make our voices interesting are often the very things that cannot be neatly generated from a prompt. If we constantly rely on the same tools to tell us what to think and how to express it, we risk losing the differences that make [...] I am not asking anyone to abandon AI. I use it, and I recognize the benefits it provides. But I do think we need to become more conscientious about when we use it and what we are asking it to do for us. Let it help with the tedious tasks. Let it serve as a resource. But do not let it become a substitute for your own intellectual development.

items.title: Military-made AI tool helped thwart World Cup bomb threat - Federal News Network
items.summary:
The 2026 World Cup brought more than six million spectators from around the world to more than 100 matches in 16 host cities in the U.S., Canada and Mexico over the course of two months, prompting a massive interagency effort to secure those sites using technologies like AI and drones. Two people were charged in connection with another bomb threat against FIFA during a World Cup match at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey. [...] A military-made artificial intelligence tool helped law enforcement thwart a bomb threat at the FIFA World Cup in California this summer.

The previously undisclosed incident occurred June 18, when Switzerland faced Bosnia and Herzegovina at SoFi Stadium outside Los Angeles, Army Capt. Ryan Hetrick, who leads the Pentagon’s Generative AI Task Force, said Nov. 6 at an AI event in Washington. [...] Hetrick has become one of the military’s biggest — and busiest — evangelists for AI. The GenAI Task Force travels around the globe to sit down with troops on operations floors and in the field and find AI fixes for their most pressing problems.

The article discusses the growing presence of artificial intelligence (AI) in everyday life and its implications for the workforce. Economists express concerns that AI may threaten entry-level and repetitive jobs, such as those in call centers, data entry, and junior copywriting, as these tasks are easier to automate.

Conversely, AI could also create new job opportunities, particularly in construction and manufacturing, as companies invest in data centers and chip production.

To prepare for the evolving job landscape, workers are encouraged to explore AI tools like chatbots and writing assistants to enhance their productivity and develop complementary skills. Local training programs, such as those offered by the University of South Alabama and the Alabama Community College System, provide foundational AI skills and awareness workshops.

The long-term impact of AI on jobs remains uncertain, but workers can position themselves as valuable resources by anticipating future employer needs and adapting to technological changes.

For more details, you can read the full article [here](https://www.fox10tv.com/2026/11/10/ai-your-job-threat-or-opportunity).

MOBILE, Ala. ( [WALA](https://www.fox10tv.com/)) \- Artificial intelligence is becoming a bigger part of everyday life, raising questions about what the technology could mean for workers and their jobs.

Some economists believe AI poses a particular threat to entry-level and repetitive work, including call center, data entry and junior copywriting jobs, according to The Wall Street Journal. Those tasks may be easier to automate.

Job growth in some office fields, including accounting, law and finance, has been slow, while tech and media jobs have declined since 2022. Microsoft also offered buyouts to tens of thousands of employees. Those trends do not necessarily mean AI caused the changes.

But AI could also create opportunities. A Bloomberg article points to potential job growth in construction and manufacturing as companies build data centers and produce the chips that power the technology. Some higher-skilled office workers could also benefit if AI helps them become more productive.

The long-term impact on jobs remains unclear, but workers can take steps to prepare. Exploring AI chatbots, writing assistants and other tools may help people find ways to work more efficiently and develop skills that complement the technology.

Local training options are available for people who want to learn more. The University of South Alabama offers a hands-on AI workforce training program. The Alabama Community College System also runs workshops, including the AI Community Caravan, that teach foundational AI skills and scam awareness.

Workers can also consider what skills may be valuable in the years ahead, what problems employers may need help solving and how they can become a trusted resource as technology changes.

Anthropic has launched Claude 3.5 Sonnet, the first release in the Claude 3.5 model family. This model significantly outperforms its predecessor, Claude 3 Opus, in various evaluations, offering enhanced intelligence at a competitive speed and cost. - **Vision Capabilities**: It surpasses previous models in visual reasoning tasks, such as interpreting charts and accurately transcribing text from imperfect images, making it valuable for sectors like retail and finance.
- **New Feature - Artifacts**: A new feature called Artifacts has been introduced, expanding the ways users can interact with Claude.

For more details, you can read the full article [here](https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-3-5-sonnet).

items.title: Introducing Claude 3.5 Sonnet \ Anthropic
items.summary:
[Skip to main content](https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-3-5-sonnet#main-content)

### 01Frontier intelligence at 2x the speed

- UpdateAug 28, 2025



### Consumer Terms and Privacy Policy


Today, we’re launching Claude 3.5 Sonnet—our first release in the forthcoming Claude 3.5 model family. Claude 3.5 Sonnet raises the industry bar for intelligence, outperforming competitor models and Claude 3 Opus on a wide range of evaluations, with the speed and cost of our mid-tier model, Claude 3 Sonnet.

Claude 3.5 Sonnet is now available for free on Claude.ai and the Claude iOS app, while Claude Pro and Team plan subscribers can access it with significantly higher rate limits. It is also available via the Anthropic [API](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/home), [Amazon Bedrock](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/anthropics-claude-3-5-sonnet-model-now-available-in-amazon-bedrock-the-most-intelligent-claude-model-yet/), and [Google Cloud’s Vertex AI](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/announcing-anthropics-claude-3-5-sonnet-on-vertex-ai-providing-more-choice-for-enterprises). The model costs $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens, with a 200K token context window.

![Claude model family](https://www.anthropic.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww-cdn.anthropic.com%2Fimages%2F4zrzovbb%2Fwebsite%2F1f044104447e9db6b22db3a06e45d114f50f274e-2200x1174.png&w=3840&q=75)

## Frontier intelligence at 2x the speed

Claude 3.5 Sonnet sets new industry benchmarks for graduate-level reasoning (GPQA), undergraduate-level knowledge (MMLU), and coding proficiency (HumanEval). It shows marked improvement in grasping nuance, humor, and complex instructions, and is exceptional at writing high-quality content with a natural, relatable tone.

Claude 3.5 Sonnet operates at twice the speed of Claude 3 Opus. This performance boost, combined with cost-effective pricing, makes Claude 3.5 Sonnet ideal for complex tasks such as context-sensitive customer support and orchestrating multi-step workflows.
